newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aide worried about U.S. energy dependence.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aide worried about U.S. energy dependence.

text.p: National Security Adviser Sandy Berger Thursday expressed concern about U.S. dependence on foreign energy sources and said the country must act to reduce domestic demand.

Berger, one of President Bill Clinton's top foreign policy aides, also stressed the United States' keen economic and geostrategic interest in the Caspian Sea region where there are major oil reserves.
After a speech at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies, Berger was asked if he was concerned about the increasing U.S. dependence on foreign energy.

"There has been an alarming reversal of the trends that were begun when Dr. (Zbigniew) Brzezinski and President (Jimmy) Carter were in the White House of trying to really focus attention on this question of energy dependence. We've seen those figures (of imported supplies) increase," he said.
Berger said "there's obviously an awful lot we need to do domestically to reduce our demand" but gave no suggestions.
On the supply side, he noted U.S. interest in the stability and peace in the Gulf region.
He also stressed that oil deposits in the Caspian Sea in Central Asia were among the largest in the world.
For this reason, "the relationship that we have with countries like Azerbaijan, Armenia, Georgia and the countries of Central Asia are extraordinarily important to our future," he said.

"This is an area which has not only rich resources but enormous cultural diversity, a very dedicated and quite educated population and by and large leaders who want to have not only relationships with their neighbours but also...with the West.
"I think we have a very strong geostrategic as well as economic interest in developing our relationships in that area of the world," he added.
